statement.excerpt: This means that the 900 million weekly active users of ChatGPT will remain a massive drain on the company’s finances, with only 5% or so of them opting to pay, and a projected 80% of its $20-a-month users expected to churn in 2026.

from_speaker: 900 million weekly active users of ChatGPT
will remain a massive drain on the company’s finances
only 5% or so of them opting to pay
our_interpretation: The firm forecast is that the predominantly free ChatGPT population will continue to impose a material net financial burden on OpenAI.
The 900 million users and approximately 5% paying share are supporting premises. They do not define a fixed future user population.
The 80% figure is expressly presented as a projection. Realized 80% churn is not a required outcome of the speaker's financial-burden forecast.
The financial comparison must include attributable service costs and attributable monetization, rather than infer free-user losses from company-wide losses.
The explicit 2026 date attaches to the churn projection. It does not clearly set a deadline for will remain, so the firm forecast retains an open horizon.
The ad-market discussion supplies a rationale, not an explicit if-then condition.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish a material continuing net cost attributable to the free-user population, after its attributable monetization. Interim losses corroborate the forecast but do not conclusively settle its unspecified duration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the free-user population has become sustainably self-funding or a material net contributor on a comparable cost basis. Subscriber growth, company-wide revenue or a churn figure alone is insufficient.
